sample.summary:
At seven in the morning, Wren Halloway telephones Corwin Pell at his Portland office and refuses his offer. Pell says he is not going away and points out that she does not have the money. Wren replies that he has until June 30 to collect, that he will get most of it and they will discuss the rest, but that he will not get the pier. She hangs up before he can answer. Outside, deckhand Jonah Marsh, who overheard the call through the office window, says her father would have done the same and asks how she will pay. Wren lays out her plan: every crossing, sunset cruises, charters, and selling the skiff and spare outboard, operating seven days a week through June.

Jonah says seven days cannot be run with one deckhand. Wren says she will find someone. Jonah offers to work double shifts without extra pay until she is out of debt. In a lower voice, he confirms their meeting the next day at six o'clock at the office after the last run, says he has something to show her that her father gave him to hold, and tells her not to tell anyone he is coming, including Ada. Wren agrees. Jonah goes to check the bilge, and Wren notes the brass key in her cardigan pocket.

They run four crossings that day. Wren sells eighteen sunset cruise tickets to a Bangor bus tour and posts a deckhand-wanted sign in the office window. At dusk, while locking the office, she sees her brother Tobias, thirty-one, thin and bearded, standing at the head of the pier with a duffel bag. He says she left a message and asks about the deckhand job. Wren tells him he missed the funeral. He acknowledges it and says he is here now. After a long look, Wren unlocks the office door again.
sample.synopsis: Wren refuses Pell's offer and vows to keep the pier. Jonah offers unpaid double shifts and arranges a secret meeting. Her estranged brother Tobias returns seeking the deckhand job.

cases.id: summary:9 The Papers on the Desk
cases.summary: Summary 316 words (target 200); Synopsis 28 words (cap 30); both passed the production parsers.

sample.summary:
Dell locates a manifold on a scrapped ferry in a yard outside Halifax on Thursday, but on Friday the yard sells it to an outfit from Portland that called an hour before him and paid triple. Dell tells Wren by phone; she understands who is responsible and hangs up without saying goodbye. The Margaret Ann remains at the end of the pier with a red Coast Guard tag on her wheel. The sunset cruises are cancelled and two June charters have withdrawn. Wren has sixty-four thousand dollars in the Saltmarsh Savings and Loan, short of the hundred and twenty thousand owed. On Friday evening a courier delivers Corwin Pell's original offer, retyped with one change: forgiveness of the debt now requires her signature before Monday's council vote. A yellow flag marks the line and a fountain pen is included.

Tobias arrives at six with groceries, sees the document, and objects. Wren argues that the boat is grounded, the charters are gone, and Pell controls the parts suppliers, lawyers, and probably half the council; signing would let her keep the house and boat and run from the town dock. Tobias counters that she would have no pier, no fuel, and shallow water, and invokes their father. Wren replies that their father mortgaged the pier, borrowed a hundred and twenty thousand dollars from Pell in secret, then died and left her to clean up, as she had cleaned up after Tobias. Tobias quietly says that is fair, sets down the groceries, takes his jacket, tells her to sign if she wants because it is her ledger, and leaves.

Wren watches him walk up Front Street without looking back, as he did ten years ago. She sits, uncaps the pen, and holds it over the flagged line for a long time. She then recaps it, lays it down beside the paper, and cries for the first time since March.
sample.synopsis: After Pell's allies outbid Dell for the manifold, Pell sends Wren a revised offer demanding her signature. She quarrels with Tobias, who leaves; she doesn't sign and cries.

sample.summary: The debt-and-vote line compresses cleanly and escalates on a tight clock, but the mystery line stalls: Jonah's timed promise in S3 and S5 and the Box 14 key in S2 build pressure that the jump into S6 releases without a beat, and S12 closes with that charge unspent.

firstFinding.headline: The Box 14 key is planted as a central mystery and never opened, located or mentioned again after S5
bullets: The scene ends on the hidden key and Wren's explicit vow to find the box and make her father 'explain himself'.
She never tries the post office, the Savings and Loan or the boatyard, though she later visits the bank for the cheque.
The key is last felt in her pocket in S5 and then drops out of the book.
The hook-mark mystery planted in this same scene is fully paid off in S10, which makes the key's abandonment more conspicuous.
firstFinding.recommendedAction: Either add a beat where Wren opens Box 14 (S10 is the natural place, with its contents feeding the receivables discovery or explaining the loan), or cut the key and let the hook marks carry the scene's mystery.
